title: A phone charger beats the Apollo computer every day.
hooks: What powered the first Moon landing? Hint: not a supercomputer.
A phone charger beats the Apollo computer every day.
POV: You’re watching 1969 tech beat today’s phones.
caption: When less was more, the Moon was within reach. How do we apply that today? #Apollo #TechHistory #Engineering #WomenInSTEM #SimpleSystems

beats.text: In 1969, a computer with less power than your phone's charger landed two humans on the Moon.
The Apollo Guidance Computer had about 4 kilobytes of RAM,
and it was programmed by hand, woven into copper wire by women

props.prompt: 1970s factory, women weaving copper rope memory, close-up of hands, warm lighting

beats.text: in a factory in Massachusetts, a technique engineers called rope memory.
When alarms went off seconds before landing, the software chose what to drop.
The lesson still holds today: a simple system that knows its priorities beats a powerful one that doesn't.
